items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had known both of them when they were kids dancing with the Whitman sisters show.

ctx.x: I think that Don had been in Paris before because he came to Spain with Don Redman's orchestra in 1947, and had toured Europe with that band.

Don was engaged to join the Eouard's band and we opened the club with Louie Williams as an added attraction. Louie was from the dance team of Pops and Louie. I had known both of them when they were kids dancing with the Whitman sisters show. Pops was the son of Alice Whitman who was a great top dancer and had taught both Pops and Louie how to dance. Louie also sang very well.

The club was very nice and rather exclusive as it was not in a basement as most clubs were. But it didn't stay open long, although it was successful, because they didn't have a licence to sell liquor. There was a bar in the theatre owned by the management which had a licence and the management thought that this licence was suitable for the club also. But the law didn't go along with that.
